messages.author: abc790e1a87bc50a
messages.subject: Kaliningrad, European Turkey missing
parts:
I am trying to use ggplot2 to make nicer rworldmap plots, based on the code I found here: http://editerna.free.fr/wp/?p=130

The plot generated by the code below shows that Kaliningrad (Russian part in Europe) and Thrace (European Turkey) are missing. Perhaps because of the discontinuity with the main polygon? Is there any way to make these parts reappear?

On a related note, I noticed that worldMap$NAME[207] is NA.


## load packages
library(ggplot2)
library(rworldmap)

## identify countries
worldMap <- getMap()
show <- which(worldMap$NAME %in% c("Russia", "Turkey", "Greece"))

## convert to data.frame
showCoords <-
  lapply(show,
         function(x) {
           df <- data.frame(worldMap@polygons[[x]]@Polygons[[1]]@coords)
           df$region <- as.character(worldMap$NAME[x])
           colnames(df) <- list("long", "lat", "region")
           return(df)
         })
showCoords <- do.call("rbind", showCoords)

## gplot
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = showCoords,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = region))

messages.author: af271c8777c52f76
messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] Kaliningrad, European Turkey missing
parts:
It's probably an issue with the underlying map imported from Natural
Earth (http://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/10m-cultural-vectors/10m-admin-0-countries/).
The borders are not compliant with the views of the UN General
Assembly, I already mentioned this to Andy in the past. See th
disclaimer by the people who compile Natural Earth: "Natural Earth
Vector draws boundaries of countries according to defacto status. We
show who actually controls the situation on the ground. Please feel
free to mashup our disputed area themes to match your particular
political outlook."

Natural Earth is "supported by NACIS (North American Cartographic
Information Society)". Personally I suspect that their maps often
reflect the viewpoint of (some people in) the United States :-( Hence
the fact they "forgot" Kaliningrad...

Regards,
JB

messages.author: abc790e1a87bc50a
messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] Kaliningrad, European Turkey missing
parts:
Hi all,

I found and fixed the problem. I had used `worldMap@polygons[[x]]@Polygons[[1]]@coords` , but `worldMap@polygons[[x]]@Polygons` can be a list of multiple elements, with 1 being the mainland and 2, 3, ... being islands or other areas that are not connected to the mainland. That is why there were several gaps on my original map.

The corrected code and the resulting plots are here: https://github.com/brechtdv/ggplot2-EU-map

Cheers,
Brecht
